title: Overload signal fusion and protective tripping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a robust aggregation layer that fuses multiple overload signals (HTTP 429 spikes, request timeouts, per-model error-rate windows, and resource saturation metrics) into a single protective-tripping decision for smart routing.

Scope:
- Design a weighted signal fusion algorithm (configurable per region/tier/customer) with debounce and hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Expose per-route and per-tenant thresholds + global defaults.
- Convert decisions into deterministic actions: immediate route downgrade to a cheaper compatible model variant, route to cached prefix response, send to Dedicated pool (if available), or open a circuit-breaker for N seconds.
- Emit detailed telemetry for every fusion decision (inputs, weights, decision, action) for auditing and post-incident analysis.

Out of scope for this ticket: billing changes, UI rollout of advanced tuning (UI stub will be added but full Console controls are a follow-up).
tasks: Document signal model and choose initial default weights (429s, p50/p95 latency, 5m error-rate, GPU-saturation)
Prototype fusion service: deterministic scorer + policy engine (feature-flagged)
Implement circuit open/close state machine with exponential backoff and tenant isolation
Add telemetry schema and wiring to tracing pipeline + per-decision events
Integrate with routing layer: action mapping and safe rollback hooks
Add end-to-end tests including synthetic 429/timeouts and chaos scenarios
Create Confluence runbook and update incident dashboard with new decision traces
acceptance_criteria: Fusion service computes identical decisions for identical signal sets (deterministic) in CI tests
When synthetic 429 spike is injected in region, routing downgrades to configured fallback model within 2s and circuit state is visible in telemetry
Circuit breaker prevents repeat traffic to overloaded model for configured hold window and automatically recovers after backoff
No more than 0.5% client-visible error-rate increase in baseline traffic during rollout (canary metrics)
Coverage: unit tests for scoring, integration tests for routing action, and a documented rollback path
